data.long_meaning: The name Thadiel is derived from the Hebrew words 'thadhe' (God) and 'el' (God or deity). It means 'God's righteous one' or 'God's servant'. In the Bible, the name Thaddeus (a variant of Thadiel) is given to one of the seventy-two disciples of Jesus, also known as Lebbaeus or Judas son of James. Thaddeus is described as having faith in Christ and was sent out to preach the gospel and heal the sick. Thaddeus is considered a saint in various Christian denominations and is remembered for his faith and devotion.

historical_references.reference: Thaddeus, one of the twelve apostles, was also known as Lebbaeus or Judas, the son of James. He is traditionally identified with Thaddeus of Edessa, who is believed to have carried the gospel to Armenia in the 1st century AD.

In the 4th century AD, Thaddeus of Edessa is mentioned in several early Syriac sources as the missionary who brought Christianity to the region of Edessa (present-day Urfa, Turkey) and founded the church there.
